result:
I stopped at about 13 of the 15 minutes because the last few changes all measured within noise. `final.py` scores **84.0× on the search split**, using **9 of the 24 scorer calls**. One of those calls was rejected outright by the scorer's static check (c6, below).

| | search score | my held-out seeds (local) |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | ~1.0 | 1.0 |
| first champion (c1) | 71.3 | — |
| final pick (c14 = `final.py`) | **84.0** | 25.7× on my own generator, all pairs exact |

My local speedups run lower than the scorer's because my generated inputs are harder. Both rank candidates the same way. I have no access to the real held-out split, so its score is still unknown.

**Why it's fast:**
- **Duplicates are grouped first.** Records with identical word sets get their pairs listed directly and are then handled once.
- **Sets are processed from smallest to largest.** A set of size n can only match an earlier set of size at least ⌈0.8n⌉. Each word's list of sets that contain it is trimmed from the front for good, because that lower limit only goes up.
- **Only the rarest words are looked up.** Each set looks up only its rarest n−⌈0.8n⌉+1 words, and is filed under only its rarest n−⌈8n/9⌉+1 words. Any pair that reaches 80 % must share one of those words, so no pair can be missed.
- **Only likely matches get the exact check.** The found candidates are checked with the reference's own rule, 5·|A∩B| ≥ 4·|A∪B|, so the output is exactly the reference's.
- **Sets with fewer than 5 words skip the lookup.** Two different small sets can never reach 80 % with each other, so these are only filed.
- **Rarity is estimated cheaply.** Instead of counting every word, words first seen late in the input count as rare, and words that are common in a sample of every 8th set go last.
- **Nothing is imported.** `collections` and `bisect` alone cost about 1.4 ms to import, roughly 8 % of the measured time.

**Approaches tried:**
- **Exact word counts to rank rarity (c1–c4):** 70–71.
- **Mid-prefix filing plus trimming the word lists (c3, c6/c7):** 79.4 for c7. c6 was rejected because importing `_collections` is not allowed.
- **Alphabetical word order with no counting (c9):** dropped. Even on evenly spread vocabularies it produced far more candidates to check.
- **"First seen late = rare" alone (c12):** 84.9 on search. But on a catalogue sorted by category it was 4× slower (41 ms against 9.7 ms). c13/c14 fix this with the sampled common-word set, which brings that case back to 9.7 ms for 83.3–84.0 on search. I took that small loss on purpose so unseen inputs can't hit the slow case.
- **Within noise, dropped:** counting during the grouping pass (c10), C-level `map` for grouping, and a list comprehension for the exact check (c15).

**Candidate log** (scorer calls in order):

| # | candidate | score | kept? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | c1 | 71.3 | champion |
| 2 | c3 | 70.4 | no change |
| 3 | c6 | invalid (`_collections` import not allowed) | dropped |
| 4 | c7 | 79.4 | champion |
| 5 | final (= c7) | 80.1 | confirmed |
| 6 | c11 | 82.1 | champion |
| 7 | c12 | 84.9 | dropped (4× slower on category-sorted input) |
| 8 | c13 | 83.3 | champion |
| 9 | final (= c14) | 84.0 | final pick |

**Correctness checks, all exact:** 300 small edge-case inputs and two rounds of 3,000 random tiny-vocabulary inputs, all compared with the reference; the held-out seeds; a Zipf-skewed vocabulary; and the category-sorted case.

The code is in `final.py`; the other candidates (`c1.py`–`c15.py`) and the test scripts are still in the folder.
